predictions.title: Device makers license third-party frontier models for assistants by H1 2027
predictions.body: Apple's WWDC decision to power the rebuilt Siri with a custom ~1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model, on a multi-year deal reported around $1 billion a year rather than ship its own model, is the clearest signal yet that even the most vertically integrated device maker has concluded that owning the device base and the user gateway beats owning the best model. That reframes the assistant race as a build-vs-buy decision: the frontier-training treadmill (capex, scarce researchers, the cost of falling a generation behind) is brutal for anyone whose core business is hardware or an OS, while the durable moat is the install base and the default-assistant slot that sits in front of it. Expect this to harden into the explicit default pattern - license the brain, own the gateway - across the consumer-assistant tier. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by H1 2027 at least one other major consumer-device, OS, or platform vendor whose flagship assistant is currently first-party - the strongest candidates being Samsung (Galaxy/Bixby), Amazon (Alexa), or a major automaker's in-car assistant - formally announces that its built-in assistant is powered by a licensed third-party frontier model (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, or a comparable lab) rather than a wholly in-house model, with a named lab partner and a shipping or beta build. Apple's privacy-by-topology framing - a small on-device model plus stateless server inference with PII stripped before anything reaches the licensed model - also supplies the template that makes such a deal defensible to a privacy-conscious base, lowering the bar for the next vendor to follow.

reasoning.because: Apple licensed a custom ~1.2T-param Gemini (~$1B/yr) to power rebuilt Siri instead of its own model
reasoning.given: frontier training is too costly/risky for device makers; the moat is install base + assistant slot
reasoning.so_that: another major consumer-device/OS/platform vendor licenses a third-party frontier model for its built-in assistant
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027, a named-lab assistant deal from Samsung, Amazon, or an automaker
reasoning.plain_language: Phone and gadget makers will rent a top AI brain from someone else instead of building their own, like Apple just did.

predictions.summary: Apple ran the rebuilt Siri on a licensed Google Gemini model, not its own, signaling device makers value the install base and assistant gateway over the model itself. By H1 2027 expect another major vendor - Samsung, Amazon, or an automaker - to license a third-party model for its assistant.

predictions.title: Android adds a user-selectable system-assistant slot for rival models by 2027
predictions.body: By opening the system assistant to a user-selectable model slot at WWDC - the "Search or Ask" panel that routes a query to Siri, Gemini, or ChatGPT (with Claude tested) - while pairing it with deepened App Intents and a free on-device Foundation Models framework for tool-calling and structured generation, Apple has redefined what the operating system itself owes the agent ecosystem: a swappable assistant brain, a standard way for apps to expose actions, and a no-cost local model any developer can call. Once the largest premium device base treats the assistant as a configurable slot rather than a hardwired service, the symmetric pressure on Google falls on Android, where Gemini is the default but assistant choice has historically been a fixed handoff rather than a first-class OS picker. The forward consequence is that Android promotes assistant selection to an OS-level setting that lets users route the system assistant - the Power-button/Circle-to-Search invocation and its successors - to a rival model app, not just Google's, mirroring Apple's slot. The deeper, more durable shift is on the developer side: App-Intents-style action exposure plus an on-device tool-calling framework become a pattern developers expect on every platform, so Google's App Actions / App Functions surface and on-device Gemini Nano tool-calling get repositioned as the Android-side answer to Foundation Models. Expect the assistant-slot move to be framed cautiously - couched in defaults, eligibility rules, and entitlements rather than a wide-open marketplace - because the same gateway economics that let Apple monetize two billion devices apply in reverse to Google. The falsifiable marker is an OS-level assistant-picker capability on Android, announced or shipped at Google I/O 2027 or in an Android 17-era release, that lets a user set a non-Google model app as the system assistant.

reasoning.because: WWDC made the iOS system assistant a user-selectable model slot plus a free on-device tool-call API
reasoning.given: Android keeps Gemini as a fixed default while Apple reframes the assistant as a swappable OS slot
reasoning.so_that: Google promotes assistant choice to an OS-level picker and repositions App Actions + Gemini Nano as the Android answer
reasoning.landing: by H2 2027 (Android 17 era): OS assistant-picker adds a non-Google model
reasoning.plain_language: After Apple let people pick which AI runs their phone's assistant, Android will likely add the same choice.

predictions.summary: Apple's WWDC user-selectable assistant slot and free on-device tool-calling pressure Google to make assistant choice an OS-level setting on Android, not a fixed Gemini handoff. The falsifiable marker is an OS-level picker for a non-Google assistant, at Google I/O 2027 or an Android 17-era release.

predictions.title: DOJ folds Apple-Siri Gemini payments into Google search-remedies case by Q1 2027
predictions.body: Apple's WWDC concession that the rebuilt Siri runs on a custom ~1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model, for roughly $1 billion a year, layers a second multi-billion-dollar commercial tie on top of the existing search-default payment Google already makes Apple. That earlier payment is the exact conduct at the center of the DOJ's monopolization case against Google: the court found the default-search deals unlawfully entrenched Google's dominance, and the remedies phase is still live, with Google appealing and the parties contesting how far behavioral fixes must reach. The new Siri arrangement gives the DOJ and the states a fresh, concrete data point that the two firms' entanglement is widening rather than unwinding precisely while a remedy is being designed. Expect the Antitrust Division to cite the Gemini-for-Siri deal in a post-trial remedies brief, a compliance-monitoring submission, or a new or amended civil investigative demand by the end of Q1 2027 - arguing that any decree limiting Google-Apple value transfer must reach the AI-assistant layer, not just search distribution, and treating the assistant slot as a second default that can foreclose rivals. The trigger is a formal filing or CID naming the Siri-Gemini payments; absent that on the docket by March 31, 2027, the prediction fails.

reasoning.because: Live DOJ Google remedies phase already targets Google-Apple default-search payments
reasoning.given: WWDC adds a ~$1B/yr Gemini-for-Siri tie on top of the same Google-Apple money flow
reasoning.so_that: Antitrust enforcers extend the remedy theory from search distribution to the AI-assistant default layer
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027, DOJ filing or CID naming the Siri-Gemini payments
reasoning.plain_language: Two companies already in court for paying each other now pay each other more, so regulators look harder.

predictions.summary: Apple's $1B/yr Gemini-for-Siri deal adds a second Google payment atop the search-default ties already central to the DOJ's live Google monopoly case. Expect the DOJ or state AGs to cite it in a remedies brief or civil investigative demand by Q1 2027.
